g.text: Log parsing—converting raw log messages into structured templates—is a
critical prerequisite for system reliability engineering (He et al., 2020).
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=1) Log parsing—converting raw log messages into structured templates—is a critical prerequisite for system reliability engineering (He et al., 2020).

g.text: Accurate parsing enables downstream tasks such as anomaly detection,
incident triage, and root cause analysis by aggregating logs into stable
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) Accurate parsing enables downstream tasks such as anomaly detection, incident triage, and root cause analysis by aggregating logs into stable event types.

g.text: However, log templates inevitably drift over time as software systems evolve
through updates, configuration changes, and new deployments, silently
breaking parsing pipelines and causing operational failures.
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) However, log templates inevitably drift over time as software systems evolve through updates, configuration changes, and new deployments, silently breaking parsing pipelines and causing operational failures.

g.text: Recent advances in large language models have enabled a new paradigm for log
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) Recent advances in large language models have enabled a new paradigm for log parsing.

architecture that separates parsing into induction (generating
natural-language rules from sample logs) and deduction (applying
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) LogRules (Huang et al., 2025) introduces a particularly promising architecture that separates parsing into induction (generating natural-language rules from sample logs) and deduction (applying rules to parse new logs).

g.text: This design achieves strong accuracy while reducing inference costs by using
g.title: N6 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) This design achieves strong accuracy while reducing inference costs by using a smaller model for deduction.

g.text: LogRules: no rule-update policy for drift
However, LogRules and similar approaches focus on initial parsing
performance and do not address a critical operational question:
how should the rule repository be updated when template drift
g.title: N7 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, LogRules and similar approaches focus on initial parsing performance and do not address a critical operational question: how should the rule repository be updated when template drift occurs?

g.text: The intuitive response to drift is to regenerate the entire rule
g.title: N8 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) The intuitive response to drift is to regenerate the entire rule repository from post-drift examples.

g.title: N9 [Result] (cites=0) Surprisingly, our experiments reveal that this Rewrite strategy performs poorly—achieving only marginally better accuracy than using stale rules unchanged.

g.text: We hypothesize that global rewriting under limited post-drift
evidence causes the LLM to inadvertently modify rules that remain
effective for stable templates, introducing regressions that
g.title: N10 [Limitation] (cites=0) We hypothesize that global rewriting under limited post-drift evidence causes the LLM to inadvertently modify rules that remain effective for stable templates, introducing regressions that offset gains on drifted templates.

g.text: We propose Patch, a conservative update policy that generates a small set of
delta rules targeting drifted patterns and prepends them to the unchanged
g.title: N11 [Method] (cites=0) We propose Patch, a conservative update policy that generates a small set of delta rules targeting drifted patterns and prepends them to the unchanged original repository.

g.text: This approach mirrors the stability-plasticity principle from continual
g.title: N12 [Method] (cites=1) This approach mirrors the stability-plasticity principle from continual learning (Wang et al., 2023).

g.text: On a synthetic drift benchmark, Patch achieves 0.2742 overall FGA,
outperforming Rewrite by +8.1 percentage points, with the largest
gains on drifted templates (+14.1 points) while also improving
g.title: N13 [Result] (cites=0) On a synthetic drift benchmark, Patch achieves 0.2742 overall FGA, outperforming Rewrite by +8.1 percentage points, with the largest gains on drifted templates (+14.1 points) while also improving stable-template performance (+5.5 points).

LLM log parsers and show that naive rewriting underperforms
g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We identify the rule repository update problem for LogRules-style LLM log parsers and show that naive rewriting underperforms conservative patching.

g.text: We propose Patch, which generates targeted delta rules and
prepends them to the unchanged original repository, achieving +8.1
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose Patch, which generates targeted delta rules and prepends them to the unchanged original repository, achieving +8.1 FGA improvement over Rewrite.

g.text: We analyze why Patch succeeds: it decouples drift adaptation from
stable-template handling, preserving pre-drift knowledge while
adding targeted capacity for new patterns.
